7
An astronaut on the Moon, where there is no air resistance, throws a ball. The ball’s initial velocity
has a vertical component of 8.00 m s–1 and a horizontal component of 4.00 m s–1, as shown.
initial velocity
path of ball
8.00 m s–1
4.00 m s–1
The acceleration of free fall on the Moon is 1.62 m s–2.
What will be the speed of the ball 9.00 s after being thrown?
A
6.6 m s–1
B
7.7 m s–1
C
10.6 m s–1
D
14.6 m s–1

hints: Notice the motion has two independent parts: horizontal velocity stays at $4.00 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ with no air resistance, while vertical velocity changes under Moon gravity.
Use $v_y = u_y - gt$ with $u_y = 8.00 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, $g = 1.62 \text{ m s}^{-2}$ and $t = 9.00 \text{ s}$ to find the signed vertical component at 9.00 s.
Combine the two perpendicular components at 9.00 s with Pythagoras: speed $= \sqrt{v_x^2 + v_y^2}$, using the magnitude of the negative $v_y$.
walkthrough: Horizontal motion has no acceleration because there is no air resistance, so $v_x = 4.00 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ at all times including at $t = 9.00 \text{ s}$.
Vertical motion has constant downward acceleration $g = 1.62 \text{ m s}^{-2}$. Take upward as positive with $u_y = +8.00 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
At $t = 9.00 \text{ s}$, $v_y = u_y - gt = 8.00 - (1.62 \times 9.00) = 8.00 - 14.58 = -6.58 \text{ m s}^{-1}$. The negative sign means the ball is now moving downward.
Speed is the magnitude of the resultant velocity: speed $= \sqrt{v_x^2 + v_y^2} = \sqrt{(4.00)^2 + (-6.58)^2}$ in $\text{m s}^{-1}$.
Evaluate: $(4.00)^2 = 16.0$ and $(6.58)^2 \approx 43.30$, so speed $= \sqrt{59.30} \approx 7.7 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.

A.explanation: This is the magnitude of the vertical component alone, about $6.58 \text{ m s}^{-1}$. It omits the $4.00 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ horizontal component still present.

B.explanation: This is $\sqrt{(4.00)^2+(-6.58)^2} \approx 7.7 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, the resultant of the unchanged horizontal and the updated vertical components.

C.explanation: This adds $4.00 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $6.58 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ linearly to get about $10.6 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, instead of combining perpendicular components with Pythagoras.

D.explanation: This is the change in vertical velocity $gt = 1.62 \times 9.00 \approx 14.6 \text{ m s}^{-1}$. It ignores the initial $8.00 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ upward velocity and the horizontal motion.
